files.summary: The endpoint is concise and follows a reasonable pattern, but it has a critical data integrity issue: it reads the existing `settings` JSONB column, merges it in JavaScript, and writes it back without any locking or atomic update. Under concurrent PATCH requests, the last writer wins and silently discards other concurrent updates to the same `settings` object. Additionally, there is no input validation on `placementSeasonLabel` (e.g., max length, allowed characters), and the error response for non-`college_admin` users returns 401 instead of 403, which is a minor HTTP semantics issue. The code is otherwise clean with parameterized queries and proper tenant scoping.

issues.message: Race condition in settings update: the read-then-write pattern (lines 29-35) is not atomic. Two concurrent PATCH requests will both read the same `settings` object, merge in their own `placementSeasonLabel`, and then write back. The second write will overwrite the first, silently losing the first update. This can cause data loss for any field in the `settings` JSONB column.
issues.suggestion: Use a single UPDATE with jsonb concatenation operator (||) or jsonb_set() to atomically merge the new key into the existing settings without a separate SELECT.

issues.message: No validation on `placementSeasonLabel` beyond trimming. An empty string, a string exceeding reasonable length (e.g., 10KB), or a string containing malicious content (XSS payload) will be stored directly into the JSONB settings column. This could lead to data integrity issues or stored XSS if the value is later rendered unsafely in the UI.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: require non-empty, max length (e.g., 100 chars), and optionally sanitize or reject HTML/script content.
